codes.title: Variable valve timing fault — bank 1
codes.subtitle: The engine can't adjust valve timing on one side. Performance and fuel economy will suffer until it's fixed.

codes.title: Valve timing too advanced — bank 1
codes.subtitle: Valve timing is running ahead of where it should be. Often caused by low oil pressure or a dirty oil control valve.

codes.title: Valve timing too retarded — bank 1
codes.subtitle: Valve timing is lagging behind where it should be. Dirty oil or a faulty actuator is usually the cause.

codes.title: Exhaust cam actuator fault — bank 1
codes.subtitle: The exhaust side camshaft actuator isn't responding correctly. This needs a mechanic to diagnose.

codes.title: Exhaust valve timing too advanced — bank 1
codes.subtitle: Exhaust valve timing is running ahead of where it should be. Often low oil or a sticking actuator.

codes.title: Cam and crank timing out of sync — bank 1
codes.subtitle: The crank and cam sensors are disagreeing on timing. This can cause rough running or a no-start.

codes.title: Exhaust cam and crank out of sync — bank 1
codes.subtitle: The crankshaft and exhaust cam sensors don't agree. Can cause rough idle or hard starting.

codes.title: Variable valve timing fault — bank 2
codes.subtitle: The valve timing actuator on the second cylinder bank isn't working properly.

codes.title: Valve timing too advanced — bank 2
codes.subtitle: Valve timing on the second bank is running ahead. Low oil or a dirty oil control valve is likely.

codes.title: Valve timing too retarded — bank 2
codes.subtitle: Valve timing on the second bank is lagging. Usually oil-related — check your oil level first.

codes.title: O2 sensor heater fault — upstream bank 1
codes.subtitle: The heater element inside your upstream oxygen sensor has failed. The sensor still works but takes longer to reach operating temperature.

codes.description: HO2S Heater Control Circuit Low (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
codes.title: O2 heater low voltage — upstream bank 1
codes.subtitle: The upstream O2 sensor heater circuit is reading low voltage. Usually a wiring fault or a failed sensor.

codes.description: HO2S Heater Control Circuit High (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
codes.title: O2 heater high voltage — upstream bank 1
codes.subtitle: The upstream O2 sensor heater is reading too high. Can be a short in the wiring or the sensor itself.

codes.title: O2 sensor heater fault — downstream bank 1
codes.subtitle: The heater in your downstream oxygen sensor has failed. This affects how the ECU monitors the catalytic converter.

codes.description: HO2S Heater Control Circuit Low (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
codes.title: O2 heater low voltage — downstream bank 1
codes.subtitle: The downstream O2 sensor heater circuit is reading low. Often a wiring issue or a failing sensor.

codes.description: HO2S Heater Control Circuit High (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
codes.title: O2 heater high voltage — downstream bank 1
codes.subtitle: The downstream O2 heater is reading too high. Usually a short in the wiring or the sensor.

codes.description: HO2S Heater Control Circuit Low (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
codes.title: O2 heater low voltage — upstream bank 2
codes.subtitle: The upstream O2 sensor on the second bank has a low heater circuit. Wiring or sensor replacement is likely needed.

codes.description: HO2S Heater Control Circuit High (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
codes.title: O2 heater high voltage — upstream bank 2
codes.subtitle: The O2 heater on the second bank's upstream sensor is reading too high.

codes.description: HO2S Heater Control Circuit Low (Bank 2 Sensor 2)
codes.title: O2 heater low voltage — downstream bank 2
codes.subtitle: The downstream O2 sensor on the second bank has a heater circuit fault.

codes.description: HO2S Heater Control Circuit High (Bank 2 Sensor 2)
codes.title: O2 heater high voltage — downstream bank 2
codes.subtitle: The downstream O2 sensor heater on bank 2 is reading high.

codes.title: Fuel pressure dangerously high
codes.subtitle: Your engine has too much fuel pressure. This is a safety issue — have it checked before driving further.

codes.title: Fuel pressure regulator fault
codes.subtitle: Your fuel pressure regulator isn't holding steady pressure. This affects fuel delivery and engine performance.

codes.title: Fuel pressure regulator circuit fault
codes.subtitle: The control circuit for the fuel pressure regulator is reporting an error. Needs electrical diagnosis.

codes.description: Fuel Pressure Regulator Control Circuit Low
codes.title: Fuel pressure regulator — low signal
codes.subtitle: The fuel pressure regulator control circuit is reading low. Often a wiring issue.

codes.description: Fuel Pressure Regulator Control Circuit High
codes.title: Fuel pressure regulator — high signal
codes.subtitle: The fuel pressure regulator control circuit is reading high. Often a short or a failed regulator.

codes.description: Fuel System Leak Detected — Large Leak
codes.title: Large fuel system leak detected
codes.subtitle: The ECU has detected a significant fuel system leak. Don't drive — this is a fire hazard.

codes.description: Fuel System Leak Detected — Small Leak
codes.title: Small fuel system leak detected
codes.subtitle: A small fuel leak has been detected. Get it checked soon — fuel leaks can become dangerous.

codes.title: MAF sensor circuit fault
codes.subtitle: Your mass air flow sensor is reporting an electrical problem. The engine can't measure air intake correctly.

codes.title: MAF sensor readings out of range
codes.subtitle: Your MAF sensor is working but its readings don't match what the ECU expects. A dirty sensor is the most common cause — try MAF cleaner spray first.

codes.description: Mass Air Flow Circuit Low Input
codes.title: MAF sensor reading too low
codes.subtitle: Your MAF sensor signal is weaker than it should be. Could be a dirty sensor, a wiring fault, or a failed sensor.

codes.description: Mass Air Flow Circuit High Input
codes.title: MAF sensor reading too high
codes.subtitle: Your MAF sensor is reporting more air than expected. Often a vacuum leak letting in unmetered air.

codes.title: MAF sensor signal cutting out
codes.subtitle: Your MAF sensor signal is dropping in and out. This is often a loose connector or a failing sensor.

codes.title: MAP sensor circuit fault
codes.subtitle: The manifold pressure sensor has an electrical fault. The ECU uses this to calculate the right fuel mixture.

codes.title: MAP sensor readings out of range
codes.subtitle: MAP sensor readings don't match expected values. Can cause poor fuel economy and hesitation.

codes.title: MAP sensor reading too low
codes.subtitle: The MAP sensor signal is too low. Usually a wiring fault or a failed sensor.

codes.title: MAP sensor reading too high
codes.subtitle: The MAP sensor signal is too high. Can be a vacuum leak or a failed sensor.

codes.title: MAP sensor signal cutting out
codes.subtitle: The MAP sensor signal is intermittent. Loose wiring or a failing sensor.

codes.title: Intake air temp sensor fault
codes.subtitle: The sensor measuring incoming air temperature has a fault. Affects fuel mixture calculation.

codes.title: Intake air temp readings out of range
codes.subtitle: The air temperature sensor is giving unexpected readings. Could be a faulty sensor or intake air leak.

codes.title: Intake air temp sensor — low reading
codes.subtitle: The intake air temp sensor is reading too cold. Usually a wiring fault or a failed sensor.

codes.title: Intake air temp sensor — high reading
codes.subtitle: The intake air temp sensor is reading too hot. Check the connector first — often a loose plug.

codes.title: Coolant temperature sensor fault
codes.subtitle: The coolant temp sensor has an electrical fault. Without accurate temperature readings, the ECU can't manage fuel and timing correctly.

codes.title: Coolant temp sensor readings out of range
codes.subtitle: Coolant temp readings don't match what the ECU expects. Could be a faulty sensor or a genuine cooling issue.

codes.title: Coolant temp sensor — reading too cold
codes.subtitle: The coolant sensor is reporting a very low temperature. Usually a failed sensor or wiring fault — but worth checking your coolant level too.

codes.title: Coolant temp sensor — reading too hot
codes.subtitle: The coolant sensor is reporting a very high temperature. Check your coolant level immediately — this could be real overheating.

codes.title: Coolant temp sensor signal cutting out
codes.subtitle: Coolant temp readings are dropping in and out. Loose connector or failing sensor.

codes.title: Throttle position sensor fault
codes.subtitle: Your throttle position sensor has a fault. The engine may go into limp mode to protect itself — get this checked soon.

codes.title: Throttle position sensor out of range
codes.subtitle: Throttle position readings are inconsistent. Can cause hesitation, erratic idle, or sudden power loss.

codes.title: Throttle position sensor — low signal
codes.subtitle: The throttle sensor signal is too low. Engine power may be limited until this is fixed.

codes.title: Throttle position sensor — high signal
codes.subtitle: The throttle sensor is reading too high. Can cause unintended acceleration or limp mode.

codes.description: Insufficient Coolant Temperature for Closed Loop
codes.title: Engine taking too long to warm up
codes.subtitle: Your engine is slow to reach operating temperature. Could be a stuck-open thermostat or a faulty coolant sensor.

codes.title: Upstream O2 sensor fault — bank 1
codes.subtitle: Your upstream oxygen sensor isn't working properly. The ECU is flying blind on fuel mixture — expect poor economy.

codes.description: O2 Sensor Circuit Low Voltage (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
codes.title: Upstream O2 sensor reading lean — bank 1
codes.subtitle: The upstream O2 sensor is reporting a lean reading. Could be a real lean condition, a failing sensor, or an exhaust leak near the sensor.

codes.description: O2 Sensor Circuit High Voltage (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
codes.title: Upstream O2 sensor reading rich — bank 1
codes.subtitle: The upstream O2 sensor is stuck reporting rich. Often a failing sensor or a real fuel delivery problem.

codes.description: O2 Sensor Circuit Slow Response (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
codes.title: Upstream O2 sensor slow to respond — bank 1
codes.subtitle: Your upstream O2 sensor is sluggish. As sensors age they slow down — replacement is usually the fix.

codes.description: O2 Sensor Circuit No Activity (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
codes.title: Upstream O2 sensor not responding — bank 1
codes.subtitle: The upstream O2 sensor isn't sending a signal. Likely a failed sensor or a broken heater element.

codes.description: O2 Sensor Heater Circuit Malfunction (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
codes.title: Upstream O2 heater fault — bank 1
codes.subtitle: The heater inside your upstream O2 sensor has failed. The sensor still works but is slower to close the fuel loop on cold starts.

codes.title: Downstream O2 sensor fault — bank 1
codes.subtitle: The downstream O2 sensor after the catalytic converter has a fault. Used mainly for catalyst monitoring.

codes.description: O2 Sensor Circuit Low Voltage (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
codes.title: Downstream O2 sensor reading low — bank 1
codes.subtitle: The downstream O2 sensor is reporting low voltage. Could be an exhaust leak or a failing sensor.

codes.description: O2 Sensor Circuit High Voltage (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
codes.title: Downstream O2 sensor reading high — bank 1
codes.subtitle: The downstream O2 sensor is stuck at a high reading. Usually a failing sensor.

codes.description: O2 Sensor Circuit Slow Response (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
codes.title: Downstream O2 sensor slow to respond — bank 1
codes.subtitle: The downstream O2 sensor is sluggish. On high-mileage cars this is common — the sensor has aged.

codes.description: O2 Sensor Circuit No Activity (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
codes.title: Downstream O2 sensor not responding — bank 1
codes.subtitle: The downstream O2 sensor isn't sending any signal. Likely a failed sensor.

codes.description: O2 Sensor Heater Circuit Malfunction (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
codes.title: Downstream O2 heater fault — bank 1
codes.subtitle: The heater in the downstream O2 sensor has failed.

codes.title: Upstream O2 sensor fault — bank 2
codes.subtitle: The upstream O2 sensor on the second cylinder bank has a fault.

codes.description: O2 Sensor Circuit Low Voltage (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
codes.title: Upstream O2 sensor reading lean — bank 2
codes.subtitle: The upstream O2 sensor on bank 2 is reporting lean. Could be a real lean condition or a failing sensor.

codes.description: O2 Sensor Circuit High Voltage (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
codes.title: Upstream O2 sensor reading rich — bank 2
codes.subtitle: The upstream O2 sensor on bank 2 is stuck reading rich.

codes.description: O2 Sensor Circuit Slow Response (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
codes.title: Upstream O2 sensor slow to respond — bank 2
codes.subtitle: The upstream O2 sensor on bank 2 is sluggish — a sign it's aging.

codes.description: O2 Sensor Circuit No Activity (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
codes.title: Upstream O2 sensor not responding — bank 2
codes.subtitle: No signal from the upstream O2 sensor on bank 2. Likely a failed sensor.

codes.description: O2 Sensor Heater Circuit Malfunction (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
codes.title: Upstream O2 heater fault — bank 2
codes.subtitle: The heater in the bank 2 upstream O2 sensor has failed.

codes.title: Downstream O2 sensor fault — bank 2
codes.subtitle: The downstream O2 sensor on the second bank has a fault.

codes.description: O2 Sensor Circuit Low Voltage (Bank 2 Sensor 2)
codes.title: Downstream O2 sensor reading low — bank 2
codes.subtitle: The downstream O2 sensor on bank 2 is reporting low voltage.

codes.description: O2 Sensor Circuit High Voltage (Bank 2 Sensor 2)
codes.title: Downstream O2 sensor reading high — bank 2
codes.subtitle: The downstream O2 sensor on bank 2 is stuck at a high reading.

codes.description: O2 Sensor Circuit Slow Response (Bank 2 Sensor 2)
codes.title: Downstream O2 sensor slow — bank 2
codes.subtitle: The downstream O2 sensor on bank 2 is slow to respond. Normal wear on high-mileage cars.

codes.description: O2 Sensor Circuit No Activity (Bank 2 Sensor 2)
codes.title: Downstream O2 sensor not responding — bank 2
codes.subtitle: No signal from the downstream O2 sensor on bank 2.

codes.description: O2 Sensor Heater Circuit Malfunction (Bank 2 Sensor 2)
codes.title: Downstream O2 heater fault — bank 2
codes.subtitle: The heater in the bank 2 downstream O2 sensor has failed.

codes.title: Fuel trim fault — bank 1
codes.subtitle: The ECU can't keep fuel mixture within normal limits on bank 1. Could be a sensor or fuel delivery issue.

codes.title: Engine running rich — bank 1
codes.subtitle: Your engine is getting too much fuel. Common causes are a leaking injector, a stuck-open fuel pressure regulator, or a faulty O2 sensor.

codes.title: Fuel trim fault — bank 2
codes.subtitle: The ECU can't hold fuel mixture in range on bank 2. Needs diagnosis to find the root cause.

codes.title: Engine running lean — bank 2
codes.subtitle: Bank 2 isn't getting enough fuel. Check for vacuum leaks, a dirty MAF, or a clogged fuel injector on that side.

codes.title: Engine running rich — bank 2
codes.subtitle: Bank 2 is getting too much fuel. Look for a leaking injector or a stuck fuel pressure regulator.

codes.title: Fuel temp sensor — low reading
codes.subtitle: The fuel temperature sensor is reading too low. Usually a wiring fault.

codes.title: Fuel temp sensor — high reading
codes.subtitle: The fuel temperature sensor is reporting abnormally high fuel temperature.

codes.description: Fuel Rail Pressure Sensor Circuit Malfunction
codes.title: Fuel rail pressure sensor fault
codes.subtitle: The fuel rail pressure sensor has an electrical fault. The ECU can't read actual rail pressure.

codes.title: Fuel rail pressure sensor out of range
codes.subtitle: Fuel rail pressure sensor readings are outside expected range. Can cause rough running and power loss.

codes.description: Fuel Rail Pressure Sensor Circuit Low
codes.title: Fuel rail pressure sensor — low signal
codes.subtitle: The fuel rail pressure sensor is reading too low. Could be a wiring issue or a failing sensor.

codes.description: Fuel Rail Pressure Sensor Circuit High
codes.title: Fuel rail pressure sensor — high signal
codes.subtitle: The fuel rail pressure sensor is reading too high.

codes.title: Fuel injector circuit fault
codes.subtitle: There's an electrical problem in the fuel injector circuit. The engine may run rough or misfire.

codes.title: Injector circuit fault — cylinder 1
codes.subtitle: Cylinder 1's fuel injector has an electrical fault. This can cause a misfire on that cylinder.

codes.title: Injector circuit fault — cylinder 2
codes.subtitle: Cylinder 2's fuel injector has an electrical fault.

codes.title: Injector circuit fault — cylinder 3
codes.subtitle: Cylinder 3's fuel injector has an electrical fault.

codes.title: Injector circuit fault — cylinder 4
codes.subtitle: Cylinder 4's fuel injector has an electrical fault.

codes.title: Injector circuit fault — cylinder 5
codes.subtitle: Cylinder 5's fuel injector has an electrical fault.

codes.title: Injector circuit fault — cylinder 6
codes.subtitle: Cylinder 6's fuel injector has an electrical fault.

codes.title: Injector circuit fault — cylinder 7
codes.subtitle: Cylinder 7's fuel injector has an electrical fault.

codes.title: Injector circuit fault — cylinder 8
codes.subtitle: Cylinder 8's fuel injector has an electrical fault.

codes.title: Engine overheating
codes.subtitle: Your engine is overheating. Pull over safely and let it cool down — driving further can cause serious engine damage.

codes.title: Transmission overheating
codes.subtitle: Your transmission is running too hot. Ease off and let it cool — continued driving can cause permanent damage.

codes.title: Engine overspeed detected
codes.subtitle: The engine exceeded its safe RPM limit. Check for stuck throttle or transmission problems.

codes.description: Throttle Position Sensor/Switch B Circuit Malfunction
codes.title: Throttle sensor B fault
codes.subtitle: The second throttle position sensor has a fault. Engine may go into limp mode.

codes.description: Throttle Position Sensor/Switch B Circuit Range/Performance
codes.title: Throttle sensor B out of range
codes.subtitle: The secondary throttle sensor readings are inconsistent. Can cause hesitation and erratic power delivery.

codes.description: Throttle Position Sensor/Switch B Circuit Low
codes.title: Throttle sensor B — low signal
codes.subtitle: The secondary throttle sensor is reading too low. Power may be limited.

codes.description: Throttle Position Sensor/Switch B Circuit High
codes.title: Throttle sensor B — high signal
codes.subtitle: The secondary throttle sensor is reading too high.

codes.title: Turbo overboosting
codes.subtitle: Your turbocharger is building more pressure than it should. This can damage the engine — get it checked quickly.

codes.description: Turbocharger Boost Sensor A Circuit Malfunction
codes.title: Turbo boost sensor fault
codes.subtitle: The turbocharger boost pressure sensor has an electrical fault. The engine can't read boost pressure accurately.

codes.description: Turbocharger Boost Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
codes.title: Turbo boost sensor out of range
codes.subtitle: Boost pressure sensor readings are outside expected values.

codes.description: Turbocharger Boost Sensor A Circuit Low
codes.title: Turbo boost sensor — low signal
codes.subtitle: The boost pressure sensor is reading too low. Performance will be affected.

codes.description: Turbocharger Boost Sensor A Circuit High
codes.title: Turbo boost sensor — high signal
codes.subtitle: The boost pressure sensor is reading too high.

codes.title: Turbo wastegate solenoid fault
codes.subtitle: The wastegate solenoid that controls boost pressure has a fault.

codes.title: Turbo not building enough boost
codes.subtitle: Your turbocharger isn't building the pressure it should. Could be a boost leak, a worn turbo, or a faulty wastegate.

codes.title: Multiple cylinders misfiring
codes.subtitle: More than one cylinder is misfiring at random. This usually points to a fuel delivery problem rather than individual coils — needs proper diagnosis.

codes.title: Cylinder 2 misfire
codes.subtitle: Cylinder 2 keeps misfiring. On most engines this is a worn ignition coil or fouled spark plug.

codes.title: Cylinder 3 misfire
codes.subtitle: Cylinder 3 keeps misfiring. Usually a worn coil or spark plug on that cylinder.

codes.title: Cylinder 4 misfire
codes.subtitle: Cylinder 4 keeps misfiring. Usually a worn coil or spark plug on that cylinder.

codes.title: Cylinder 5 misfire
codes.subtitle: Cylinder 5 keeps misfiring. Usually a worn coil or spark plug.

codes.title: Cylinder 6 misfire
codes.subtitle: Cylinder 6 keeps misfiring. Usually a worn coil or spark plug.

codes.title: Cylinder 7 misfire
codes.subtitle: Cylinder 7 keeps misfiring. Usually a worn coil or spark plug.

codes.title: Cylinder 8 misfire
codes.subtitle: Cylinder 8 keeps misfiring. Usually a worn coil or spark plug.

codes.title: Knock sensor fault — bank 1
codes.subtitle: Your knock sensor has a fault. The engine can't detect pinging, so it won't retard timing to protect itself.

codes.title: Knock sensor out of range — bank 1
codes.subtitle: Knock sensor readings are outside expected values.

codes.title: Knock sensor — low signal bank 1
codes.subtitle: The knock sensor signal is too low. Usually a wiring issue or a failed sensor.

codes.title: Knock sensor — high signal bank 1
codes.subtitle: The knock sensor signal is too high.

codes.title: Knock sensor fault — bank 2
codes.subtitle: The knock sensor on bank 2 has a fault.

codes.title: Knock sensor — low signal bank 2
codes.subtitle: The bank 2 knock sensor signal is too low.

codes.title: Knock sensor — high signal bank 2
codes.subtitle: The bank 2 knock sensor signal is too high.

codes.description: Crankshaft Position Sensor A Circuit Malfunction
codes.title: Crankshaft position sensor fault
codes.subtitle: Your crank sensor has a fault. The engine may stall, not start, or run very rough — this is a critical sensor.

codes.description: Crankshaft Position Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
codes.title: Crankshaft position sensor out of range
codes.subtitle: Crank sensor readings are inconsistent. Can cause stalling and hard starting.

codes.description: Crankshaft Position Sensor A Circuit Low Input
codes.title: Crankshaft position sensor — low signal
codes.subtitle: The crank sensor signal is too weak. Wiring fault or failing sensor.

codes.description: Crankshaft Position Sensor A Circuit High Input
codes.title: Crankshaft position sensor — high signal
codes.subtitle: The crank sensor signal is too strong. Wiring fault or failing sensor.

codes.description: Crankshaft Position Sensor A Circuit Intermittent
codes.title: Crankshaft position sensor signal cutting out
codes.subtitle: The crank sensor signal is intermittent. This can cause random stalling — get it fixed soon.

codes.description: Camshaft Position Sensor A Circuit Malfunction (Bank 1)
codes.title: Camshaft position sensor fault — bank 1
codes.subtitle: The cam sensor has a fault. Can cause no-start, stalling, or rough running.

codes.description: Camshaft Position Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 1)
codes.title: Camshaft position sensor out of range — bank 1
codes.subtitle: Cam sensor readings are outside expected values.

codes.description: Camshaft Position Sensor A Circuit Low (Bank 1)
codes.title: Camshaft position sensor — low signal bank 1
codes.subtitle: The cam sensor signal is too weak. Usually a wiring fault or failing sensor.

codes.description: Camshaft Position Sensor A Circuit High (Bank 1)
codes.title: Camshaft position sensor — high signal bank 1
codes.subtitle: The cam sensor signal is too high.

codes.description: Camshaft Position Sensor A Circuit Malfunction (Bank 2)
codes.title: Camshaft position sensor fault — bank 2
codes.subtitle: The cam sensor on bank 2 has a fault.

codes.description: Camshaft Position Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 2)
codes.title: Camshaft position sensor out of range — bank 2
codes.subtitle: Bank 2 cam sensor readings are outside expected values.

codes.title: EGR system fault
codes.subtitle: Your exhaust gas recirculation system isn't working correctly. Mainly an emissions issue but can cause rough idle over time.

codes.title: EGR flow too low
codes.subtitle: Not enough exhaust gas is being recirculated. On older diesels this is often a clogged EGR valve — cleaning it sometimes fixes it.

codes.title: EGR flow too high
codes.subtitle: Too much exhaust gas is being recirculated. Can cause rough idle and poor performance.

codes.title: EGR circuit electrical fault
codes.subtitle: The EGR valve control circuit has an electrical problem.

codes.title: EGR circuit out of range
codes.subtitle: The EGR circuit readings are outside expected range. Usually a stuck or dirty EGR valve.

codes.description: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Sensor A Circuit Low
codes.title: EGR position sensor — low signal
codes.subtitle: The EGR position sensor is reading too low. Wiring fault or failed sensor.

codes.description: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Sensor A Circuit High
codes.title: EGR position sensor — high signal
codes.subtitle: The EGR position sensor is reading too high.

codes.description: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Sensor B Circuit Low
codes.title: EGR sensor B — low signal
codes.subtitle: EGR sensor B is reading too low.

codes.description: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Sensor B Circuit High
codes.title: EGR sensor B — high signal
codes.subtitle: EGR sensor B is reading too high.

codes.description: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Sensor A Circuit Malfunction
codes.title: EGR sensor A fault
codes.subtitle: The EGR sensor A has an electrical fault.

codes.title: Secondary air injection fault
codes.subtitle: The secondary air injection system has a fault. Mainly an emissions issue on petrol engines.

codes.title: Secondary air injection flow problem
codes.subtitle: The air injection system isn't flowing correctly.

codes.description: Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve A Circuit Malfunction
codes.title: Air injection switching valve fault
codes.subtitle: The secondary air injection switching valve has a fault.

codes.title: Catalytic converter losing efficiency — bank 1
codes.subtitle: Your catalytic converter on bank 1 is no longer cleaning exhaust gases efficiently. On older cars this is normal wear — it will eventually need replacing.

codes.description: Warm Up Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 1)
codes.title: Warm-up catalyst efficiency low — bank 1
codes.subtitle: The warm-up catalyst on bank 1 is losing efficiency. Similar to P0420 but refers to the smaller pre-cat.

codes.title: Main catalyst efficiency low — bank 1
codes.subtitle: The main catalytic converter on bank 1 needs attention.

codes.title: Catalytic converter losing efficiency — bank 2
codes.subtitle: Your catalytic converter on bank 2 is no longer efficient. Usually normal aging on high-mileage cars.

codes.description: Warm Up Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 2)
codes.title: Warm-up catalyst efficiency low — bank 2
codes.subtitle: The warm-up catalyst on bank 2 is losing efficiency.

codes.title: Main catalyst efficiency low — bank 2
codes.subtitle: The main catalytic converter on bank 2 needs attention.

codes.title: EVAP system fault
codes.subtitle: Your fuel vapour capture system has a fault. This is an emissions issue — check your fuel cap is properly tightened first.

codes.description: Evaporative Emission Control System Incorrect Purge Flow
codes.title: EVAP purge flow problem
codes.subtitle: The fuel vapour isn't purging correctly. Often a faulty purge valve.

codes.description: Evaporative Emission Control System Leak Detected (Small Leak)
codes.title: Small fuel vapour leak detected
codes.subtitle: A small leak in the evaporative system. First check your fuel cap — a loose cap often sets this code.

codes.description: Evaporative Emission Control System Purge Control Valve Circuit
codes.title: EVAP purge valve circuit fault
codes.subtitle: The EVAP purge control valve has an electrical fault.

codes.description: Evaporative Emission Control System Purge Control Valve Circuit Open
codes.title: EVAP purge valve — open circuit
codes.subtitle: The purge valve circuit is open. Usually a wiring fault or failed valve.

codes.description: Evaporative Emission Control System Purge Control Valve Circuit Shorted
codes.title: EVAP purge valve — shorted circuit
codes.subtitle: The purge valve circuit has a short.

codes.description: Evaporative Emission Control System Vent Control Circuit
codes.title: EVAP vent valve circuit fault
codes.subtitle: The EVAP vent valve has an electrical problem.

codes.description: Evaporative Emission Control System Vent Control Circuit Open
codes.title: EVAP vent valve — open circuit
codes.subtitle: The vent valve circuit is open.

codes.description: Evaporative Emission Control System Vent Control Circuit Shorted
codes.title: EVAP vent valve — shorted circuit
codes.subtitle: The vent valve circuit has a short.

codes.description: Evaporative Emission Control System Vent Valve/Solenoid Circuit
codes.title: EVAP vent solenoid fault
codes.subtitle: The EVAP vent solenoid has a circuit fault.

codes.description: Evaporative Emission Control System Pressure Sensor Malfunction
codes.title: Fuel tank pressure sensor fault
codes.subtitle: The fuel tank pressure sensor has a fault. Needed for the ECU to check for vapour leaks.

codes.description: Evaporative Emission Control System Pressure Sensor Range/Performance
codes.title: Fuel tank pressure sensor out of range
codes.subtitle: Tank pressure sensor readings are outside expected values.

codes.description: Evaporative Emission Control System Pressure Sensor Low
codes.title: Fuel tank pressure sensor — low reading
codes.subtitle: The tank pressure sensor is reading too low.

codes.description: Evaporative Emission Control System Pressure Sensor High
codes.title: Fuel tank pressure sensor — high reading
codes.subtitle: The tank pressure sensor is reading too high.

codes.description: Evaporative Emission Control System Leak Detected (Gross Leak)
codes.title: Large fuel vapour leak detected
codes.subtitle: A significant leak has been found in the fuel vapour system. Check your fuel cap and fuel tank area.

codes.description: Evaporative Emission Control System Leak Detected (Very Small Leak)
codes.title: Very small fuel vapour leak
codes.subtitle: A tiny leak in the EVAP system. Start by checking the fuel cap.

codes.description: Evaporative Emission Control System Leak Detected (Fuel Cap)
codes.title: Fuel cap not sealing properly
codes.subtitle: Your fuel cap isn't sealing. Tighten it until it clicks — if the code comes back, replace the cap.

codes.title: Vehicle speed sensor fault
codes.subtitle: Your vehicle speed sensor has a fault. Speedometer readings may be wrong and the transmission may shift oddly.

codes.title: Vehicle speed sensor out of range
codes.subtitle: Speed sensor readings are inconsistent. Speedometer and transmission may be affected.

codes.title: Vehicle speed sensor — low signal
codes.subtitle: The speed sensor signal is too weak.

codes.title: Vehicle speed sensor — erratic signal
codes.subtitle: The speed sensor signal is cutting in and out or spiking.

codes.title: Idle control system fault
codes.subtitle: Your idle control system has a fault. Expect rough or erratic idle speed.

codes.description: Idle Control System RPM Too Low
codes.title: Idle speed too low
codes.subtitle: Engine idle is lower than it should be. Could be a dirty throttle body or a fault in the idle control valve.

codes.description: Idle Control System RPM Too High
codes.title: Idle speed too high
codes.subtitle: Engine idle is higher than it should be. Often caused by a vacuum leak or a faulty idle air control valve.

codes.title: Idle control circuit — low signal
codes.subtitle: The idle control circuit is reading low.

codes.title: Idle control circuit — high signal
codes.subtitle: The idle control circuit is reading high.

codes.title: Electrical system voltage fault
codes.subtitle: The ECU is seeing abnormal voltage. Check your battery and alternator.

codes.title: Electrical system voltage unstable
codes.subtitle: Voltage is fluctuating more than it should. Often a failing alternator or bad battery connection.

codes.title: Low system voltage
codes.subtitle: Electrical system voltage is too low. Check your battery charge and alternator output. A weak battery is the most common cause.

codes.title: High system voltage
codes.subtitle: Electrical system voltage is too high. Usually a failing voltage regulator in the alternator.

codes.description: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input A Circuit
codes.title: Cruise control input fault
codes.subtitle: There's a fault in the cruise control input circuit.

codes.title: ECU communication fault
codes.subtitle: There's a communication problem between engine control units. Needs specialist diagnosis.

codes.description: Internal Control Module Memory Check Sum Error
codes.title: ECU memory error
codes.subtitle: The engine control unit has a memory fault. This needs specialist attention.

codes.title: ECU programming fault
codes.subtitle: The ECU has a programming error. Needs specialist reprogramming or replacement.

codes.description: Internal Control Module Keep Alive Memory (KAM) Error
codes.title: ECU keep-alive memory error
codes.subtitle: The ECU's keep-alive memory has a fault. This stores learned settings — they may be lost.

codes.description: Internal Control Module Random Access Memory (RAM) Error
codes.title: ECU RAM fault
codes.subtitle: The ECU has a RAM fault. Needs specialist diagnosis.

codes.description: Internal Control Module Read Only Memory (ROM) Error
codes.title: ECU ROM fault
codes.subtitle: The ECU's read-only memory has an error. Usually requires ECU replacement.

codes.title: ECU processor fault
codes.subtitle: The engine control unit's processor has a fault. Specialist diagnosis required.

codes.title: ECU performance fault
codes.subtitle: The ECU isn't performing within expected parameters.

codes.title: Alternator control circuit fault
codes.subtitle: The alternator control circuit has a fault. Charging system may not be working properly.

codes.title: Charge warning light circuit fault
codes.subtitle: There's a fault in the charge warning light circuit.

codes.title: Alternator field circuit fault
codes.subtitle: The alternator field circuit has a fault. Battery may not be charging correctly.

codes.description: Sensor Reference Voltage A Circuit Open
codes.title: Sensor reference voltage fault
codes.subtitle: The 5V reference voltage supply to sensors has an open circuit. Multiple sensors may be giving wrong readings.

codes.description: Sensor Reference Voltage B Circuit Open
codes.title: Sensor reference voltage B fault
codes.subtitle: The second sensor reference voltage circuit has an open fault.

codes.title: Glow plug module fault
codes.subtitle: The glow plug control module has a fault. Hard cold starts are likely on this diesel engine.

codes.title: Glow plug fault — cylinder 1
codes.subtitle: Cylinder 1's glow plug has a fault. Cold starting may be harder, especially in cool weather.

codes.title: Glow plug fault — cylinder 2
codes.subtitle: Cylinder 2's glow plug has a fault. Cold starts will suffer.

codes.title: Glow plug fault — cylinder 3
codes.subtitle: Cylinder 3's glow plug has a fault.

codes.title: Glow plug fault — cylinder 4
codes.subtitle: Cylinder 4's glow plug has a fault.

codes.title: Glow plug fault — cylinder 5
codes.subtitle: Cylinder 5's glow plug has a fault.

codes.title: Glow plug fault — cylinder 6
codes.subtitle: Cylinder 6's glow plug has a fault.

codes.title: Glow plug fault — cylinder 7
codes.subtitle: Cylinder 7's glow plug has a fault.

codes.title: Glow plug fault — cylinder 8
codes.subtitle: Cylinder 8's glow plug has a fault.

codes.title: Transmission control system fault
codes.subtitle: Your transmission control system has detected a fault. The gearbox may shift differently or go into limp mode.

codes.title: Transmission control out of range
codes.subtitle: Transmission control system readings are outside expected values.

codes.title: Transmission control electrical fault
codes.subtitle: There's an electrical problem in the transmission control system.

codes.description: Torque Converter/Brake Switch B Circuit Malfunction
codes.title: Brake switch circuit fault
codes.subtitle: The brake switch circuit used by the transmission has a fault.

codes.title: Transmission range sensor fault
codes.subtitle: The sensor that tells the ECU which gear you're in has a fault. The car may not start or may behave unpredictably.

codes.title: Transmission range sensor out of range
codes.subtitle: Gear position readings are inconsistent.

codes.description: Transmission Fluid Temperature Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
codes.title: Transmission fluid temp sensor out of range
codes.subtitle: Transmission fluid temperature sensor readings are off.

codes.description: Transmission Fluid Temperature Sensor Circuit Low
codes.title: Transmission temp sensor — low reading
codes.subtitle: The transmission fluid temp sensor is reading too low.

codes.description: Transmission Fluid Temperature Sensor Circuit High
codes.title: Transmission temp sensor — high reading
codes.subtitle: The transmission fluid temp sensor is reading too high. Check your transmission fluid level.

codes.title: Transmission input speed sensor fault
codes.subtitle: The sensor measuring how fast the torque converter turbine is spinning has a fault.

codes.title: Transmission input speed sensor out of range
codes.subtitle: Turbine speed sensor readings are inconsistent.

codes.description: Input/Turbine Speed Sensor Circuit No Signal
codes.title: Transmission input speed sensor — no signal
codes.subtitle: The turbine speed sensor isn't sending a signal.

codes.title: Transmission output speed sensor fault
codes.subtitle: The sensor measuring gearbox output speed has a fault.

codes.title: Transmission output speed sensor out of range
codes.subtitle: Output speed sensor readings are inconsistent.

codes.description: Output Speed Sensor Circuit No Signal
codes.title: Transmission output speed sensor — no signal
codes.subtitle: No signal from the transmission output speed sensor.

codes.title: Engine speed signal fault — transmission
codes.subtitle: The transmission control unit isn't receiving a valid engine speed signal.

codes.title: Wrong gear ratio detected
codes.subtitle: The transmission is achieving a different gear ratio than expected. Could be a worn clutch pack or hydraulic issue.

codes.title: First gear ratio incorrect
codes.subtitle: First gear isn't engaging properly or the ratio is wrong.

codes.title: Second gear ratio incorrect
codes.subtitle: Second gear ratio is off. May slip or shift poorly.

codes.title: Third gear ratio incorrect
codes.subtitle: Third gear ratio is off.

codes.title: Fourth gear ratio incorrect
codes.subtitle: Fourth gear ratio is off.

codes.title: Fifth gear ratio incorrect
codes.subtitle: Fifth gear ratio is off.

codes.title: Torque converter clutch fault
codes.subtitle: The torque converter clutch isn't engaging or releasing correctly. May cause shudder at highway speeds.

codes.description: Torque Converter Clutch Circuit Performance or Stuck Off
codes.title: Torque converter clutch stuck off
codes.subtitle: The torque converter clutch is stuck in the off position. This hurts fuel economy on the highway.

codes.description: Torque Converter Clutch Circuit Stuck On
codes.title: Torque converter clutch stuck on
codes.subtitle: The torque converter clutch is stuck on. Can cause stalling when stopping.

codes.title: Torque converter clutch electrical fault
codes.subtitle: The torque converter clutch circuit has an electrical problem.

codes.title: Transmission pressure solenoid A fault
codes.subtitle: The transmission pressure control solenoid A has an electrical fault.

codes.title: Transmission shift solenoid A fault
codes.subtitle: Shift solenoid A isn't working correctly. Gear changes may be erratic or stuck.

codes.description: Shift Solenoid A Performance or Stuck Off
codes.title: Shift solenoid A stuck off
codes.subtitle: Shift solenoid A is stuck in the off position.

codes.title: Shift solenoid A stuck on
codes.subtitle: Shift solenoid A is stuck on.

codes.title: Shift solenoid A electrical fault
codes.subtitle: An electrical fault in shift solenoid A's circuit.

codes.title: Transmission shift solenoid B fault
codes.subtitle: Shift solenoid B isn't working. Affects which gears the transmission can select.

codes.description: Shift Solenoid B Performance or Stuck Off
codes.title: Shift solenoid B stuck off
codes.subtitle: Shift solenoid B is stuck off.

codes.title: Shift solenoid B stuck on
codes.subtitle: Shift solenoid B is stuck on.

codes.title: Shift solenoid B electrical fault
codes.subtitle: An electrical fault in shift solenoid B's circuit.

codes.title: Transmission shift solenoid C fault
codes.subtitle: Shift solenoid C has a fault.

codes.description: Shift Solenoid C Performance or Stuck Off
codes.title: Shift solenoid C stuck off
codes.subtitle: Shift solenoid C is stuck off.

codes.title: Shift solenoid C stuck on
codes.subtitle: Shift solenoid C is stuck on.

codes.title: Shift solenoid C electrical fault
codes.subtitle: An electrical fault in shift solenoid C.

codes.title: Transmission shift solenoid D fault
codes.subtitle: Shift solenoid D has a fault.

codes.title: Transmission shift solenoid E fault
codes.subtitle: Shift solenoid E has a fault.

codes.title: Transmission shift fault
codes.subtitle: The transmission is having trouble shifting. Could be hydraulic, electrical, or mechanical.

codes.description: Transfer Case Control System MIL Request
codes.title: Transfer case control warning
codes.subtitle: The transfer case control system has requested a warning light. Relevant to 4WD vehicles.

codes.title: Clutch pedal switch fault
codes.subtitle: The clutch pedal position switch has a fault. The car may not start or the cruise control may not work.

codes.description: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch A Circuit
codes.title: Transmission fluid pressure sensor fault
codes.subtitle: The transmission fluid pressure sensor has a fault.

codes.title: Transmission fluid pressure too low
codes.subtitle: Transmission fluid pressure is critically low. Check your transmission fluid immediately — driving further can cause serious damage.

codes.title: Transmission control unit power fault
codes.subtitle: The transmission control unit isn't getting enough power.

codes.title: Drive motor A fault
codes.subtitle: The main drive motor has a performance fault. Needs specialist hybrid diagnosis.

codes.description: Drive Motor A Phase U Current
codes.title: Drive motor current fault
codes.subtitle: The drive motor phase current has a fault.
